text: As rho increases toward 1 (staying below the ESP boundary), the reservoir's linear memory capacity:
choices: stays constant, because MC depends only on N and not on rho
decreases toward zero, because the reservoir becomes unstable
increases without bound, eventually exceeding N
increases and saturates near its upper bound N
explanation: Higher rho lengthens memory, so MC rises as rho -> 1^- and approaches (but never exceeds) the Jaeger bound MC <= N; the sweep shows MC saturating near N. MC clearly depends on rho (not just N), does not collapse until rho passes 1 and the ESP is lost, and can never exceed N.
